channel.title: doyouknow.app - English
channel.description: Surprising facts about UAE, Saudi Arabia, and the world.

item.title: Cairo Metro Guide: Lines, Tickets, and Tips
item.description: The Cairo Metro was the first metro system in Africa and the Middle East. Here is how its lines, tickets, and women-only cars work.

item.title: Opening a Bank Account in Egypt: Guide
item.description: How foreign residents can open a bank account in Egypt: required documents, choosing a bank, account types, and practical tips for expats and long-term visitors.

item.title: Egypt Driving Guide: Rentals & Road Rules
item.description: Should you rent a car in Egypt? Car rental requirements, an International Driving Permit, road conditions, and why most visitors use drivers instead in 2026.

item.title: Mobile Wallets in Egypt: How They Work
item.description: Mobile wallets like Vodafone Cash and InstaPay have grown fast in Egypt as digital alternatives to cash for everyday payments.

item.title: How Remittances Work and Why They Matter
item.description: Remittances are money sent home by people working abroad, moving through banks, money transfer operators, and mobile wallets.

item.title: Nile Cruise Guide: Luxor to Aswan Trip Planning
item.description: How to plan a Nile cruise between Luxor and Aswan: cruise length options, what's included, choosing a ship, temple stops, and practical booking tips for 2026.

item.title: What Is Mada, Saudi Arabia's National Payment Network?
item.description: Mada is Saudi Arabia's domestic debit card network, regulated by SAMA, used for most in-store and online card payments in the Kingdom.

item.title: How Saudi Traffic Fines Work: A Practical Guide
item.description: How Saudi Arabia enforces traffic violations through the Saher camera system, points, and how to check and pay fines via Absher.

item.title: Understanding Insulin Resistance
item.description: Insulin resistance means cells respond poorly to insulin, forcing the pancreas to work harder, and is a key step toward type 2 diabetes.

item.title: Understanding the Sandwich Generation
item.description: The sandwich generation refers to adults simultaneously raising children and caring for aging parents, often under real financial strain.

item.title: Are Superfoods Real, or Just Marketing?
item.description: The word superfood has no official scientific definition. It is a marketing term for nutrient-dense foods, not a category regulators recognize.

item.title: What Is a Gap Year, and Is It Worth It?
item.description: A gap year is a planned break from formal study, often used for travel, work, or volunteering, before continuing education or a career.

item.title: What Is Cloud Computing, Explained Simply?
item.description: Cloud computing means renting computing power, storage, and software over the internet instead of running your own servers.

item.title: What Is the Diriyah Gate Project?
item.description: Diriyah Gate is a Saudi giga-project redeveloping the historic At-Turaif UNESCO site into a heritage, culture, and hospitality district.

item.title: What Is Dropshipping and How Does It Work?
item.description: Dropshipping lets a store sell products it never stocks, with the supplier shipping directly to the customer instead.

item.title: What Is Emotional Resilience?
item.description: Emotional resilience is the ability to adapt and recover from stress and setbacks, a skill that can be strengthened rather than a fixed trait.

item.title: What Is Glycemic Load? Glycemic Index vs. Load
item.description: Glycemic load adjusts the glycemic index for actual portion size, giving a more realistic picture of a food's effect on blood sugar.

item.title: What Is King Salman Park in Riyadh?
item.description: King Salman Park is a PIF giga-project in central Riyadh built around a huge new urban park, cultural venues, and a botanical garden.

item.title: What Is Microlearning?
item.description: Microlearning breaks lessons into short, focused chunks, often just a few minutes long, designed to fit into small pockets of time.

item.title: What Is Permissive Parenting?
item.description: Permissive parenting combines high warmth with few rules or limits, one of four parenting styles first described by psychologist Diana Baumrind.
